answer.summary: Ries defines an MVP by its learning purpose: find the most efficient way to test a hypothesis and learn whether it is true—not simply build a stripped-down product. It should help surface important problems early enough to respond.

sections.heading: Purpose of an MVP
sections.content: For the hypothesis being tested, an MVP is the most efficient way to get the validation needed to determine whether that hypothesis is true. Ries says it is not inherently a bare-bones or low-quality product tactic; the right test depends on customer expectations in the market.

sections.heading: Why learn early
sections.content: Ries also describes the essence of an MVP as finding out as soon as possible about a potentially catastrophic problem, while there is still time to do something about it. He recommends containing the downside of mistakes and, for example, asking 10 customers to use the product and say what is awful.
